editorial:
Imagine being so checked out of your own life that you ignore your family for a board game. That is where you meet Branko, a wealthy guy who cares more about chess and his mistress than his wife, Visnja. The movie sets up a cold, distant feeling right from the start. You can tell their marriage is basically over before the real drama hits. While on a train trip, Branko leaves Visnja all alone just to play a game of chess in another car. This one selfish choice leads to a nightmare when three men attack her in her compartment. It is a heavy setup that makes you feel angry at the main character for his lack of care.

What really works here is how the movie handles the guilt and the fallout. The acting is solid, and it does not shy away from the dark reality of the crime. Some parts feel a bit slow, but it helps you feel the weight of the situation. If you like gritty crime dramas that focus on human mistakes, you should check this out. It is best to grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture quality, or you can try renting it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. Just be ready for a very emotional ride.
endingExplained: The movie ends with Branko facing the total collapse of his world. After the attack, his guilt eats him alive because he knows he caused the tragedy by leaving Visnja alone. He tries to fix things, but the damage is too deep. The story wraps up with him realizing that his life is like a lost game of chess. He is left alone with his regrets, showing that some mistakes can never be undone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gritty dramas about guilt and family secrets.
